brief: A three-storey tower: drawers on the bottom storey and open bins on the top storey.

requirements.evidence: Full hex bases stacked at (0,0) levels 0, 1, 2 with a second column at (-1,0) levels 0-2; the tower is three storeys tall (levels 0-2).
Two classic drawers (drawer:0#1,0#cut and drawer:0#2,0#cut) on level 0, set on the cut faces of half-n bases at (1,0,0) and (2,0,0).

requirements.requirement: Open bins on the top storey
requirements.evidence: Two full-depth open bins (bin:0,0,2~hex-bin-full and bin:-1,0,2~hex-bin-full) sit in the top-storey cells at level 2; their tops are open.

finish.summary: Built a three-storey tower: a bottom storey with two classic drawers on half-base cut faces, a middle storey of solid bases, and a top storey with two open full-depth bins. Joint bolts lock the column, and open faces are capped per house rules. check_build is clean with meshClash clear, 69 parts in total. The top bins are open trays, not closed; no props were added since the brief did not ask for them.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
